calls.raw: {"changes": [{"action": "replace", "number": 2, "question": {"type": "mcq", "text": "Which statement about branch coverage is true?", "options": ["Achieving full branch coverage guarantees full statement coverage.", "Branch coverage requires testing each individual condition separately.", "Branch coverage is weaker than statement coverage.", "Branch coverage ignores the true/false outcomes of decisions."], "answer": 0, "answer_text": "Achieving full branch coverage guarantees full statement coverage.", "topic": "Branch coverage", "origin": "from_material", "source": 1, "explanation": "Full branch coverage forces both outcomes of every decision to be executed, which necessarily executes every statement in the program."}}, {"action": "remove", "number": 3}, {"action": "add", "question": {"type": "short", "text": "Why might a test suite that achieves branch coverage still miss bugs that depend on specific condition combinations?", "suggested_answer": "Because branch coverage only ensures each decision's true and false outcomes are executed, it does not require testing all possible combinations of the individual conditions within a decision, so faults that arise from particular condition interactions can remain undetected.", "topic": "Branch coverage", "origin": "from_material", "source": 1, "explanation": "Branch coverage checks decision outcomes but not the internal condition logic, leaving condition‑coverage gaps."}}]}
